title: Launch
description: Opportunity launched on a Delta II 7925H from Cape Canaveral, 7 July 2003, 20:18:15 PDT.

time.note: A launch is observed on Earth, so event and observation time coincide.

title: Landing in Eagle crater, Meridiani Planum
description: Opportunity bounced at least 26 times on its airbags and came to rest inside a small impact crater later named Eagle, about 14.9 km from its target point.

time.note: NASA gives 21:05 PST 24 Jan = 04:54 UTC 25 Jan without saying whether this is spacecraft or Earth-received time. MER counts the touchdown sol as Sol 1.

title: Out of Eagle crater
description: Opportunity drove out of Eagle crater.

title: Heat Shield Rock
description: Opportunity found a basketball-sized rock, named Heat Shield Rock, that turned out to be an iron-nickel meteorite.

title: Arrival at Victoria crater
description: Opportunity reached Victoria crater, about 800 m across.

title: Arrival at Endeavour crater
description: Opportunity reached the rim of Endeavour crater, about 22 km across.

title: The darkest sky: tau about 10.8
description: In Perseverance Valley, Pancam images taken through 440 nm and 750 nm filters pointed at the Sun were used to estimate the atmospheric opacity: a tau of about 10.8 — only a tiny amount of sunlight reached the ground.

time.note: Caption: "around 9:33 a.m. PDT" (= 16:33 UTC); it also prints "12:33 a.m. EDT", which does not match. Not stated whether this is spacecraft or Earth-received time.

title: Last communication
description: A severe Mars-wide dust storm blanketed the rover's location; Opportunity stopped communicating with Earth.

title: End of mission
description: NASA declared the end of the Opportunity mission.
